decisions.question: The refine phase has completed. Please review the analysis and approve to continue, or provide feedback to request changes.
decisions.resolution:
{"action": "approve", "context": "## Resolved decisions

- D1 (decompose deliverables): **single umbrella** — ship all 4 MCP tools + 2 skills in #1759 together.
- D2 (skill location): **skills/ alongside existing** — no operator/agent subtree split yet.
- D3 (submit_task task-id reuse): **defer** — tracked separately as #1804.
- D4 (rebuild_and_rollout): **include in scope** — #1763 has merged, unblocking the implementation.
- D5 (log persistence for agent-diagnose): **defer** — tracked separately as #1805; agent-diagnose ships against currently-available data.
- D6 (network-isolation probe image): **reuse sandbox image** — short-lived Job, delete after results.
- D7 (tool ownership): **orchestrator-owned** — new routes under orchestrator/routes/; matches existing pattern.

## Resolved feedback (feedback-1)

- Q1 (operator persona): egg developer running `make redeploy` on local k3s. No prod architecture yet. Skills can assume single-cluster / single-namespace / kubectl-context-resolves-to-egg-system.
- Q2 (identifier-translation asymmetries catalogue): Pod UID ↔ Job UID (#1760, #1764); session token ↔ container_id; issue number ↔ pipeline_id ↔ branch name (#1773); task_id ↔ agent role ↔ container name; contract field path `decisions.N` vs bare `decisions` (#1801 analysis).
- Q3 (existing integration tests): keep alongside the new MCP tool; don't migrate. Docker runtime is still supported for local dev; separate substrate.
- Q4 (deployment-diagnose silent-failure scan shape): scan **both** gateway + orchestrator; signature matching via structured-fields first with hash-of-stripped-line fallback; burst threshold 3+ in any 60s window; last ~2000 lines; human-invoked only (not continuous/automatic).
- Q5 (submit_task reuse fix shape): surface as known concern; specific fix tracked in #1804. No action in this umbrella.
- Q6 (other deployment environments): k3s only for day 1.
- Q7 (prune_stale_worktrees confirmation): `dry_run` is a sufficient gate for the local-dev persona. No extra confirmation needed.
- Q8 (existing ops runbook): none exists; skills bootstrap from the #1759 validation session's commentary.

## Note added during review

- Overlap between the proposed `deployment-diagnose` / `agent-diagnose` skills and the existing overseer agent is real (both are watchers that detect anomalies, classify them, and report to a human). Filed as #1806 — investigation, non-blocking for #1759. Implementation plan should reference #1806 so the skills and the overseer don't get built in isolation and patched together later."}

pr.title: Add Kubernetes deployment-diagnostic MCP tools and skills (#1759)
pr.description:
Adds the MCP surface for diagnosing Kubernetes deployments on k3s — five new orchestrator tools and two operator-side skills that compose them — so future validation sessions have structured diagnostics instead of raw kubectl fallbacks.

Tools: get_deployment_context, validate_deployment_manifests, prune_stale_worktrees, validate_network_isolation, rebuild_and_rollout. Skills: deployment-diagnose, agent-diagnose. All under @require_lifecycle_secret. Skills redact env + log tails via orchestrator/redaction.py.

Closes #1759.
